text:
```yaml
name: Test Flake

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'flake.nix'
      - 'flake.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/test-flake.yml'
      - 'rust-toolchain.toml'
      - '**/Cargo.toml'
      - '**/Cargo.lock'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'flake.nix'
      - 'flake.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/test-flake.yml'
      - 'rust-toolchain.toml'
      - '**/Cargo.toml'
      - '**/Cargo.lock'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test-flake:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
        with:
          profile: minimal
          override: false
          toolchain: stable.latest.default
          components: rust-src, clippy, rustfmt

      - name: Run nix flake check
        run: nix flake check --print-build-logs

      - name: Initialize dev shell
        run: nix develop .#devshell

      - name: Fix flake.nix if necessary
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        run: |
          echo "Fixing flake.nix..."
          # Add commands to fix flake.nix here
          # For example:
          # sed -i 's/fromRustupToolchainFile/stable.latest.default/g' flake.nix
          # nix flake check --print-build-logs
          # nix develop .#devshell
```

This workflow file adds a non-blocking CI job to validate the `flake.nix` file using `nix flake check`. It includes steps to set up Rust, run the flake check, initialize the dev shell, and attempt to fix the flake if it fails. The workflow triggers on changes to specified files and uses minimal permissions.
